nutshell: For a fiddler, South Florida is thin, seasonal and tilted north. A metro of roughly 6 million people has one weekly Irish session (Tim Finnegan's, Delray Beach), one seasonal one (McCarthy's, Tequesta, September-May) and none in Miami-Dade or Broward. The best weekly fiddle night is an old-time jam, running since about 1996, that now meets every Thursday in the Fiddlershop, a national violin retailer in Pompano Beach. Around it sit a bluegrass association founded in 1971 with free weekly and monthly jams, one healthy monthly contra in Boca Raton ($15), more modern western square dancing than contra, and plenty of Israeli folk dance. Snowbirds set the calendar: sessions swell November-April and some shut for the summer. The region's living folk life is Caribbean and Latin American: Haitian konpa and folkloric drumming, Bahamian Junkanoo, Trinidadian steelpan and Afro-Cuban bata. Its fiddle claim to fame is 'Orange Blossom Special', whose writer lived and died here.

Bluegrass (South Florida Bluegrass Association, 1971; Everglades Bluegrass Festival)

Haitian konpa and folkloric dance with live drumming (Little Haiti)
Trinidadian/pan-Caribbean carnival and steelpan (Miami Broward Carnival, Panorama)
Modern western square dancing and Israeli folk dance
top10: thesession.org shows only one active Irish session within 60 km of Fort Lauderdale (Tim Finnegan's, Delray Beach) and none within 60 km of Miami (https://thesession.org/sessions/3406).

Irish trad runs on snowbird time: McCarthy's in Tequesta ended for the summer on 31 May 2026 and restarted 10 Sep; Tim Finnegan's 'cranks up to speed' November-April with visitors from Boston, Chicago, New York, Canada, Ireland and England (https://thesession.org/sessions/9621).
The longest-running trad jam is old-time (c. 1996), now every Thursday at the Fiddlershop in Pompano Beach, a national online violin retailer with 12 luthiers (https://www.oldtimejammers.com/).

'Orange Blossom Special' writer Ervin T. Rouse bought a Miami house in 1938 and died in Miami-Dade in 1981 after years fiddling for tips in taverns at the edge of the Everglades (https://www.ncpedia.org/rouse-ervin-t).

Irish fiddler James Kelly, TG4 Gradam Ceoil 2006 and composer of 800+ tunes, has lived in Miami since 1984 (https://museumofmiami.org/south-florida-folklife-center/artist-in-residence-programs/james-kelly/).
Modern western squares beat contra four weekly nights to one monthly dance, including challenge-level C-1/C-2 and the LGBTQ+ South Florida Mustangs (1977) (http://www.southfloridamustangs.org/).
Lomax, Hurston and Barnicle recorded in Belle Glade in 1935, and the WPA recorded Bahamian 'Conch' songs in Riviera (now Riviera Beach) in 1940 (https://www.loc.gov/item/flwpa000080/).
Joni Mitchell was 'discovered' at Coconut Grove's Gaslight South in 1967 when Bobby Ingram brought David Crosby to hear her (https://www.bocamag.com/when-coconut-grove-was-groovy/).

The heritage scene dwarfs the Anglo-Celtic one: Sounds of Little Haiti draws 800-1,200 people a month and the Miami Broward Carnival drew 100,000+ in 2025 (https://haitiantimes.com/2025/09/19/sounds-of-little-haiti-10-year-anniversary/).

There is no regular shape-note singing anywhere in South Florida; the first seed singing was held in Miami Shores on 10 Oct 2026 (https://shapenotesingings.com/singings/miami-shores-half-day-singing).
character: South Florida's Anglo-Celtic folk world is a small, retiree-heavy, seasonal subculture inside a metro whose living folk traditions are Caribbean and Latin American. Who shows up: retired educators at the Delray Irish session, snowbirds from Boston, Chicago, New York, Canada and Ireland in winter, daytime library and senior-center jammers, a 1977 gay square-dance club, Kings Point retirees doing Israeli dances, singer-songwriters at song swaps, and a few UM students playing newgrass. For a fiddler the signature traditions are the Thursday old-time jam at the Fiddlershop, the 1971 bluegrass association and the song swap; for the metro as a whole they are Haitian konpa and folkloric drumming, Bahamian Junkanoo, steelpan carnival and Afro-Cuban bata. Activity is scattered along about 100 miles of I-95 with no central neighborhood like 1960s Coconut Grove: Palm Beach County is strongest for tunes, Broward for bluegrass and song swaps, Miami-Dade for heritage. Gentrification keeps pushing heritage communities outward, as the Bahamian West Grove's Goombay spawns a Broward spin-off in Miramar.

Calle Ocho venues advertise rumba: Cubaocho lists 'son, rumba, salsa and Latin jazz'; Ball & Chain runs 'Salsero Sundays'. No verified community rumba in a street or park on a fixed schedule; one 2025 blog claims congas in Domino Park, unsourced. Mostly staged nightlife.

14ymedio (May 2017): 'every Sunday dozens of poets' at Rancho Bejucal held guateques broadcast on Channel 41; poet Roberto Garcia lives in Homestead. CiberCuba 2023: an improvisation 'batalla' between Lenier Mesa and Juan Antonio Diaz. HistoryMiami archive: 1996 punto guajiro recording at the Dade County Youth Fair. Punto cubano was inscribed by UNESCO in 2017. No 2024-26 evidence of a specific peña; controversias in Hialeah not verified.

No changui ensemble or tres luthier found. A danzon evening was held at MDC's Koubek Center in 2018 (Community News headline). NEA bio notes Cachao (NEA 1995) innovated in danzon and settled in Miami in 1983.

timeline.event: Tequesta live on Biscayne Bay (Miami-Dade) and north into Broward to at least Pompano Beach; few survivors by 1763.
Coconut Grove established (incorporated 1919); Miami's oldest continuously inhabited neighborhood.
Bahamian settlers build Coconut Grove before Miami's incorporation; Bahamian-style raised houses and sponge fishing (1890s) recorded by Bucuvalas.
Miami incorporated; 168 of 362 voters counted as 'colored' (Wikipedia; other sources 162/368 or 'one-third'); Black residents then confined to 'Colored Town' (Overtown).
Lyric Theatre opens in Overtown; NW 2nd Ave becomes the 'Little Broadway of the South' hosting Basie, Ella, Calloway, Holiday, Nat King Cole.
Seaboard Air Line's Orange Blossom Special train begins New York-Miami service (to early 1960s).
Alan Lomax, Zora Neale Hurston and Mary Elizabeth Barnicle record in Eatonville, Belle Glade and Chosen (Belle Glade and Chosen are in Palm Beach County); 227 discs total (AFC 1935/001).
Lomax and Barnicle record 149 discs in the Bahamas.
Ervin T. Rouse writes 'Orange Blossom Special' and buys a house in Miami.
Ervin and Gordon Rouse make the first recording of 'Orange Blossom Special'.
Stetson Kennedy and Robert Cook record Bahamian/African American material in Riviera (Riviera Beach, Palm Beach County) and Key West for the Florida WPA.
Ukrainian Dancers of Miami founded by Taras Maksymovich.
Bill Monroe (with fiddler Chubby Wise) popularizes 'Orange Blossom Special'.
South Florida Emerald Society founded March 17, 1949 by ten Irish-American businessmen.
Sullivan and Iola Pugh form the Miami Soul Stirrers gospel trio.
Florida Folk Festival begins in White Springs (outside MSA).
First post-revolution Cuban exile wave ('Golden Exile').
Vince Martin settles in Coconut Grove (1960); Fred Neil follows after 1962 meeting; David Crosby discovers the Grove (c.1962).
Coconut Grove Arts Festival begins as a 'little clothesline arts fair' (now ~120,000 attendance).
Johnny Cash's 'Orange Blossom Special' hit; Cash later brings Rouse to play at a Miami concert.
Freedom Flights bring an estimated 300,000 Cubans to Miami.
Lovin' Spoonful's 'Coconut Grove' (John Sebastian), a tribute to Fred Neil.
David Crosby hears Joni Mitchell at the Gaslight South, Coconut Grove; takes her to California.
'1968 Pop and Underground Festival' at Gulfstream Park, Hallandale; ~25,000; promoters incl. Ric O'Barry and Michael Lang.
Miami Pop Festival, Gulfstream Park; ~100,000; Joni Mitchell, Ian & Sylvia, Flatt & Scruggs, Junior Junkanoos, Buffy Sainte-Marie.
Doors concert at Dinner Key Auditorium, seen as 'beginning of the end' of bohemian Grove.
Fred Neil and Ric O'Barry found the Dolphin Project; Gaslight closed by 1970; Tomás Granado forms norteño conjunto in Homestead.
South Florida Bluegrass Association founded New Year's Day; chartered Sept 1971 (Bill Caudill first president).
Seminole Tribal Fair & Pow Wow begins (50th edition Feb 2023, Hollywood). Exact first year unverified.
First Miccosukee Indian Arts & Crafts Festival (50th anniversary Dec 2024).
Goombay Festival founded in Coconut Grove (1976 per FIU/Herald; 1977 per WLRN/Spotlight).
First Everglades Bluegrass Convention held 'in the Glades', headlined by Bill Monroe; Ralph Stanley the next year.
Calle Ocho festival started by Cuban exiles in Little Havana.
Mariel boatlift: ~125,000 Cubans and ~25,000 Haitians; batá master Ezequiel Torres arrives.
Ervin Rouse dies in Miami-Dade (date disputed); Fred Neil's last public performance at the Old Grove Pub.
Irish fiddler James Kelly moves permanently from Dublin to Miami.
Florida Folk Heritage Awards begin; Jan Mapou founds Sosyete Koukouy in Miami.
South Florida Folklife Festival (3 editions) at Metro-Dade Cultural Center plaza; Historical Museum of Southern Florida with Florida Folklife Program.
Calle Ocho conga line of 119,986 sets a Guinness record.
Libreri Mapou opens in Little Haiti.
South Florida Folk Festival inception (per club); founded by WLRN folk DJ Michael Stock / Broward Folk Club.
Balsero crisis: ~35,000 Cuban rafters.
Israel 'Cachao' López named NEA National Heritage Fellow.
Calle Ocho cancelled after Brothers to the Rescue shootdown; Luna Star Café opens in North Miami.
Epstein Brothers (klezmer, retired to Tamarac) receive Florida Folk Heritage Award (1997) and NEA Heritage Fellowship (1998).
Haitian Compas Festival founded in Miami (medium confidence).
Bamboo Room roots club opens in Lake Worth.
James Kelly receives Florida Folk Heritage Award; Fred Neil dies at Summerland Key (outside MSA).
James Kelly named TG4 Gradam Ceoil Irish Musician of the Year.
Cachao dies in Coral Gables; South Florida Folk Festival returns after 2-year gap (Markham Park); Bamboo Room's first closure.
Ezequiel Torres named NEA National Heritage Fellow.
Goombay suspended (to 2022); Bamboo Room's original owners exit.
Rhythm Foundation hosts weekly contra dance nights at North Beach Bandshell (caller Anita Mason, band Cornbread).
Bobby Ingram, 'dean' of the Grove folk scene, dies (September); ~600 at memorial.
COVID: Calle Ocho permit denied (cancelled 2020-21); SFFF moves to Bergeron Rodeo Grounds, Davie.
South Florida Folk Festival held virtually (Feb 13-14).
Calle Ocho returns; West Grove renamed 'Little Bahamas'; South Florida Fair Old Time Fiddle Contest begins (inferred from 5th annual in 2026).
Goombay revived after 2014-2022 hiatus; 50th Seminole Tribal Fair & Pow Wow.
Library of Congress AFC grant to FIU to document Goombay; Bamboo Room reopens as Rudy's at Bamboo (Feb 14; sixth grand opening); FFHA to Ukrainian Dancers of Miami, Papaloko, Marisol Blanco.
Luna Star Café founders retire after 29 years and pass the venue to Brie Kelley and Eric King; Goombay co-founder Herb Hiller dies (Feb 3); Goombay June 6-8, ~20,000 projected.
5th Old Time Fiddle Contest at South Florida Fair (Jan 25); 49th Everglades Bluegrass Festival scheduled Dec 11-13 at Greynolds Park; SFFF announces Feb 5-7, 2027.

surprises: Only one active Irish session lies within 60 km of Fort Lauderdale and none near Miami, and the only other one in the MSA (McCarthy's, Tequesta) shuts for the summer (https://thesession.org/sessions/9621).

The writer of 'Orange Blossom Special', Ervin T. Rouse, owned a Miami house from 1938 and died in Miami-Dade in 1981 after years fiddling for tips at the edge of the Everglades (https://www.ncpedia.org/rouse-ervin-t).

TG4 Gradam Ceoil winner James Kelly has lived in Miami since 1984, yet there is no Irish session south of Delray Beach (https://museumofmiami.org/south-florida-folklife-center/artist-in-residence-programs/james-kelly/).

The metro's longest-running trad jam (c. 1996) is old-time, not Irish, and meets in the showroom of a national online violin retailer, the Fiddlershop in Pompano Beach (https://www.oldtimejammers.com/).

Broward's folk hub is an aquaponic tilapia farm: the SFBA's weekly bluegrass jam and the folk club's monthly song swap both meet at Together We Stand in Hollywood (https://www.southfloridabluegrass.com).
Modern western square dancing outnumbers contra, including challenge-level C-1/C-2 squares and the LGBTQ+ South Florida Mustangs, founded 1977 (http://www.caller4u.com/).
In January 1940 the WPA recorded Bahamian 'Conch' songs from an 84-year-old blind Bahamian-born man at the Gospel Hall in Riviera, now Riviera Beach (https://www.loc.gov/item/flwpa000080/).
Zora Neale Hurston's 1939 WPA railroad spiking songs came from Max Ford, a singing liner on a construction gang near Miami around 1930 (https://www.loc.gov/item/flwpa000003/).
A metro of about 6 million has no regular shape-note singing; the first seed singing was held in Miami Shores on 10 Oct 2026 (https://shapenotesingings.com/singings/miami-shores-half-day-singing).

The region's only folk radio is one two-hour Sunday show (Michael Stock, WLRN, since 1981), cut by an hour in 2025 months before Stock entered the Folk Radio Hall of Fame (https://palmbeachartspaper.com/folk-radio-hall-of-fame-inducts-longtime-wlrn-host-stock/).

Only three NEA National Heritage Fellows have ever been listed in the metro (Cachao, the Epstein Brothers, Ezequiel Torres), and none is Seminole, Miccosukee, Haitian or Bahamian (https://www.arts.gov/honors/heritage/ezequiel-torres).

Two diaspora genres practised here are on UNESCO's intangible heritage lists: Cuban punto (2017) and Haitian konpa (Dec 2025) (https://haitiantimes.com/2025/12/11/unesco-konpa-intangible-heritage-haiti/).

Goombay drew about 500,000 at its 1980s-90s peak and now survives on about $143,000 of City of Miami money with no private sponsors (https://coconutgrovespotlight.com/2026/06/01/can-a-revived-goombay-stand-on-its-own/).

Florida's only mariachi conservatory, in Homestead, teaches about 300 farmworkers' children a year for free (https://www.wlrn.org/arts-culture/2024-11-06/making-mariachi-cool-floridas-only-conservatory-in-homestead-shares-music-mexican-american-pride).
North Palm Beach County (Jupiter and Tequesta) has more trad-tune sessions than all of Miami-Dade (https://flafiddlers.wordpress.com/regular-jams/).

There is no sea-shanty sing in a maritime metro, no klezmer jam in a heavily Jewish one, and no Miami builder in the international Cuban tres luthier directory (http://www.cubantresguitar.com/tres-luthiers.html).
Flatt & Scruggs and the Junior Junkanoos shared the December 1968 Miami Pop Festival bill with Joni Mitchell (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Pop_Festival_(December_1968)).
Israeli folk dance may be the metro's most frequent folk dance form, much of it in the Kings Point retirement community's ballroom in Delray Beach (https://www.gifd.org/event.aspx?idarea=18).
The Bamboo Room roots club in Lake Worth Beach has had six grand openings since 1999 (https://palmbeachartspaper.com/lake-worth-beachs-bamboo-room-returns-and-gets-back-to-its-musical-roots/).

The Ukrainian Dancers of Miami (founded 1941) predate the Cuban exile by nearly two decades (https://dos.fl.gov/cultural/programs/florida-folklife-program/folk-heritage-awards/list-of-past-recipients/the-ukrainian-dancers-of-miami/).
surprises_all_threads: thesession.org shows exactly ONE active Irish session within 60 km of Fort Lauderdale (Tim Finnegan's, Delray Beach), and nothing within 60 km of Miami, a metro of about 6 million. The only other active listing in the MSA is McCarthy's in Tequesta at the far north end of Palm Beach County.

Irish trad here runs on snowbird time. McCarthy's session literally shuts for the summer (ended 31 May 2026, resumed 10 Sep 2026); Tim Finnegan's 'cranks up to speed' November-April with visitors from Boston, Chicago, NY, Canada and Ireland; the 2006-13 Luna Star session died because it couldn't stay lit out of season.
The metro's longest-running trad instrumental jam is old-time, not Irish: the Oldtime Jammers (c.1996), who now meet every Thursday at the Fiddlershop violin store in Pompano Beach.

The South Florida Bluegrass Association's weekly jam meets at an aquaponic tilapia farm in Hollywood (Together We Stand). The SFBA's Everglades Bluegrass Festival reaches its 49th year in December 2026.

Square dancing outnumbers contra about 4 weekly sessions to 1 monthly dance. It includes challenge-level C-1/C-2 squares and the LGBTQ+ South Florida Mustangs (founded 1977, 50th gala March 2027) in Wilton Manors, plus $6 city-run Plus and Advanced dances in Boynton Beach.

Israeli folk dance may be the most frequent folk dance form: Ira Weisburd teaches Mon/Thu/Sat (plus 'NuLine' Wed) inside the Kings Point retirement community in Delray, and the JCCs and synagogues add more nights.

No English country dance, morris, sword, shape-note singing, Scandinavian dance, Balkan group, klezmer jam or Québécois veillée could be found, despite large Jewish and French-Canadian snowbird populations. Klezmer appears only as concerts.

North Palm Beach County (Jupiter/Tequesta) outdoes all of Miami-Dade for trad tunes: a Monday library old-time jam, a Sunday Celtic/old-time/Portland Collection session and the seasonal McCarthy's Irish session, against Miami's one monthly old-time jam.
SASSF turned its 40+-year Highland Games (born 1983 in the old Key Biscayne zoo) into a Celtic music festival in 2026.
Contra prices rose to $15 in September 2026, the most expensive regular trad activity here; nearly every jam is free.

South Florida's only folk/bluegrass/Celtic specialty radio is one 2-hour Sunday show (Michael Stock, WLRN, since 1981), trimmed from 3 hours in early 2025, months before Stock entered the Folk Radio Hall of Fame (Nov 2025). Stock also seeded the folk festival and club.
No regular Sacred Harp singing exists anywhere in South Florida (nearest regular: Orlando). The first seed singing was Oct 10, 2026 in Miami Shores, led by visiting scholar Esther Morgan-Ellis.
Broward's folk hub is a tilapia-powered aquaponic farm: SFBA's weekly bluegrass jam and SFFAMC's monthly song swap both meet at Together We Stand in Hollywood.

Fiddlershop, a major national online violin retailer (12 luthiers, ~6,000 setups/yr), is in Pompano Beach and hosts a bluegrass fiddle weekend, yet no weekly old-time or Irish fiddle teaching circle was found locally.
The SFBA (chartered 1971) is older than almost every other folk institution in the metro; the Everglades Bluegrass Festival has run every year since 1978.
The Flick's site, where Joni Mitchell was told she couldn't make it singing only her own songs, is now Titanic Brewery, hosting weekly blues and jazz jams.
The Bamboo Room has had six grand openings since 1999.
No sea-shanty sing in a maritime metro, and no Miami builder in the international Cuban tres luthier directory (nearest: Tampa).
The region's only verified fiddle contest (South Florida Fair Old Time Fiddle Contest) began only around 2022.
A University of Miami Frost newgrass band (The Wire Jays) formed to earn ensemble credit went viral with a bluegrass Justin Bieber cover.

In January 1940 the WPA recorded Bahamian 'Conch' songs at the Gospel Hall in Riviera (now Riviera Beach), Palm Beach County, from an 84-year-old blind Bahamian-born man, his wife and his daughter. About 25 items are streaming on loc.gov.

Only three NEA National Heritage Fellows have ever been listed in the metro: Cachao (1995), the Epstein Brothers (1998, klezmer retirees in Tamarac) and Ezequiel Torres (2010). None are Seminole, Miccosukee, Haitian or Bahamian.
Two diaspora genres practised in Miami are on UNESCO's intangible heritage lists: Cuban punto (2017) and Haitian konpa (Dec 2025).

Goombay drew about 500,000 at its 1980s-90s peak, went dormant after 2014 and was revived in 2022. It now depends almost entirely on City of Miami money ($143k in 2026). The LOC put a new online collection documenting it on the web in Sep 2026, and a Broward spin-off began in Miramar in 2026.
Florida's only mariachi conservatory is in Homestead, serving farmworker children for free. It grew from 20 to 300 students a year after opening in 2015.
Hurston's 1939 WPA railroad songs came from a Miami construction-gang singing liner, Max Ford, around 1930.
The Ukrainian Dancers of Miami (founded 1949) predate the Cuban exile.
HistoryMiami is now the Museum of Miami, and FIU's Cuban Research Institute now calls itself the Institute for Cuban Studies. Old names in links and citations go stale.
Sounds of Little Haiti, a free monthly konpa night, has drawn an estimated 250,000 people since 2015.
A weekly Haitian folkloric dance class with live drumming costs $0-15, which makes it one of the most accessible heritage practices in the metro.

'Orange Blossom Special' — the fiddler's anthem — was written by a man who bought a Miami house in 1938 and died in Miami-Dade in 1981 after years fiddling for tips in Everglades-edge taverns (NCpedia).

One of Ireland's top fiddlers, James Kelly (ex-Planxty/Patrick Street, TG4 Musician of the Year 2006, 800+ compositions), has lived in Miami since 1984 — yet thesession.org lists zero tunes named for Miami or Florida's southern places.

Lomax, Hurston and Barnicle recorded in Belle Glade and Chosen (Palm Beach County) in June 1935, and Kennedy & Cook recorded Bahamian material in Riviera (Riviera Beach) in 1940 — the metro's northern edge is in the canonical LOC field recordings, while Miami itself is not.

Bill Monroe headlined the first Everglades Bluegrass Convention (1977-78); the South Florida Bluegrass Association has run since New Year's Day 1971 and its newsletter is on Library of Congress microfilm. The 49th festival is Dec 2026.
A brand-new (c.2022) Old Time Fiddle Contest at the South Florida Fair explicitly rules that 'the Devil went down to Georgia' is not a traditional fiddle tune and welcomes Irish fiddling.
Only 8 NEA Heritage Fellows are listed for Florida; 3 are metro-linked: Cachao (1995), the klezmer Epstein Brothers who retired to Tamarac (1998), and batá master Ezequiel Torres (2010).
The December 1968 Miami Pop Festival (100,000) — billed as the East Coast's first major rock festival — booked Flatt & Scruggs and the Junior Junkanoos alongside the Grateful Dead.
The Ukrainian Dancers of Miami have performed since 1941, making them one of Miami's oldest continuous traditional dance troupes.

data_quality_notes:
Four threads were merged; ten recurring events appearing in two threads were deduplicated, giving 58 in-MSA events (about 147/month; about 20/month are strict fiddle-tune sessions). Two contradictions were resolved by re-fetching sources: the 2026 South Florida Folk & Acoustic Music Festival was the 36th (Miami New Times), not the 39th; the Ukrainian Dancers of Miami were founded in 1941 and first performed in 1949 (FFHA bio), while the Museum of Miami gives 1949. Unresolved: folk festival founding (early 1990s; 1991-94 depending on source), contra admission ($15 SFCDS vs $10 SFFAMC newsletter), Penny Lane beginner jam (weekly vs April only), Together We Stand address (57th Dr vs Ave), Tim Finnegan's address (1725 vs 2885 S Federal Hwy), Goombay founding (1976 vs 1977), Miccosukee festival (1974 vs 1975), Compas Festival (1998 vs 1999), Sosyete Koukouy (1965 movement vs 1985 Miami), SFBA founding and Everglades Bluegrass numbering, Rouse's death date (3 vs 8 July 1981) and the 1896 vote count. All threads were search-rate-limited, so Facebook/Instagram-only groups, Palm Beach venues, gospel quartets, Haitian church choirs and college radio are undercounted. Several sites blocked scripts or are dead (timfinnegansirishpub.com, Kings Point PDFs, israelidances.com, Florida Memory, historymiamiarchives.org, tunearch.org; tirnamblath.com and browardfolkclub.org dead; miamibrowardcarnival.com hijacked). thesession 'nearby' hides dead listings, contradancelinks is frozen around 2021, and Israeli-dance listings are undated. AI search summaries made errors (1935 trip as WPA; Celia Cruz and Myrlande Constant as NEA fellows), and some heritage facts rest only on news headlines. Seasonal per-month figures are annual averages.

[trad-dance] thesession.org 'nearby' (radius 60) returns only active listings: 1 for Fort Lauderdale, 2 for West Palm, 1 for Miami. Older listings (Luna Star, Frog & Toad, O'Shea's, Flying Turtles) appear only in text search and are dead. At radius 200 the next sessions are Vero Beach, Fort Myers, Melbourne and Venice. Tim Finnegan's address differs between sources: 1725 S Federal Hwy (old Florida Irish Pipers page) vs 2885 S Federal Hwy (FSFA, Feb 2026). thesession coordinates (26.428,-80.072) fit the 2885 address. Start time drifted from 16:00 (2013) to 15:00 (2019) to 13:00 (2021-2025). The Florida Irish Pipers' current session list omits every South Florida session, while their older page listed Tim Finnegan's. Lists drift. contradancelinks.com's Florida page is frozen at about January 2021 and lists dead venues (Michael's Body Scenes, Hollywood Woman's Club, Coral Gables, Earth 'N Us Farm, the Keys). The A-Jacks and Castoffs club pages still carry COVID-era vaccination notices; the City of Boynton Beach class page (2026 skip dates) is the current evidence. Israeli-dance listings (israelidances.com, gifd.org) are undated, and israelidances.com returns 403 to scripts. Only Temple Beth Am (Apr 2026) carries a dated instance, and Soref JCC has a live but undated program page. SFBA founding is ambiguous: sfbahistory.org's footer says 'Copyright ... 1971', the site shows 'SFBA 1978', the festival numbering implies a first Everglades festival in 1978, and '31 years' at Ives Dairy to 2008 implies 1977. McCarthy's times are inconsistent: 17:00-19:00 (Feb 2026, FSFA) vs 17:00-20:00 (Sep 2026 restart notice). Several sources could not be machine-read: tirnamblath.com (DNS dead), timfinnegansirishpub.com (403), Facebook/Instagram (Tír na mBláth, @miamioldtime), Kings Point PDFs (403). Confidence was lowered accordingly. Jamfinder.org data comes from its public Supabase table as read by its own map (info_as_of Oct 2026, with source refs); it helped confirm several jams. Coordinates come from thesession.org, Jamfinder, or OSM Nominatim (1-2 s spacing). Kings Point Delray, Levis JCC and The Field were not geocoded and are left null. per_month for seasonal events is an annual average (e.g. McCarthy's 2/month x 9/12 = 1.5; Long Key 4.33 x 3/12 = 1.08). Ira Weisburd's Kings Point sessions are 'seasonal only' but stated at in-season frequency because the season length isn't published. The web-search tool was heavily rate-limited during this run, so coverage of Facebook-only groups (Irish set dancing, Québécois clubs, Greek and Balkan) is probably incomplete.

[song-media] SFFAMC recurring-events page (modified 2026-09-26) is the main source for open mics; some entries are self-flagged as uncertain, and listings conflict with venue sites (Village Music every Thursday vs 1st & 3rd; FUN West Regional 3rd vs 4th Thursday; Project Sirena 2nd Wednesday vs a Sunday in Oct 2026). Bergeron Rodeo Grounds address appears as both 4201 SW 65th Way and 4261 NW 65th Way. SFBA free festival listed 1-5pm but the Nov 2026 lineup starts 12:00. Festival founding year inferred (36th annual in 2026 -> ~1991). Web search quota was shared and heavily rate-limited; coverage of Palm Beach County venues, Black gospel quartet practice, Haitian church choirs, WXEL and college radio (WRGP, WVUM) is thin. Gospel quartet names returned by a search summary were unverifiable and excluded. Rudy's Pub founding: own site says Feb 14, 2011; ArtsPaper says 2012 (and downstairs location since 2018). Melo Groove article and Main Street Cafe 'opened six years ago' article are undated. Together We Stand geocoded to street level only; The Field and River of Grass UU not geocoded. Luna Star open mic (last Saturdays) and Arts Garage open mic are not confirmed on the venues' own sites. Florida Ukulele Network membership (500+) comes from a search summary of artscalendar.com and was not directly fetched.

[heritage] Goombay founding year conflicts: 1976 (LOC blog 2024) vs 1977 (festival site, Coconut Grove Spotlight 2025, LOC blog 2026). Used 1977. Sosyete Koukouy founding: 60th anniversary in Dec 2025 implies 1965; Mapou's narrative places the Haiti radio raid in 1969; FFHA says he founded it in Miami in 1985. Treated as one movement with the Miami chapter dated 1985. Haitian Compas Festival: 'turns 25' in 2023 (Herald headline) vs '27th annual' in 2025, so first edition in 1998 or 1999. Seminole Tribal Fair 2026 dates: flyer and powwows.com say Jan 30-31; schedule page says Jan 30-Feb 1. Founding year not verified (a 1973 Florida Memory photo was reported but returned HTTP 403). Several founding years are inferred from edition numbers (Miccosukee 51st, Lebanese 47th, St. Catherine 49th, Calle Ocho 48th, Festival Maya 14th, SF Folk Festival 39th, bomba festival '3rd'); gaps such as the COVID years would shift these. Wikipedia's National Heritage Fellowship list misattributes years when parsed by section; arts.gov profiles are authoritative. The arts.gov state filter returns HTTP 410 to scripts, so all 502 profiles were scraped individually. Name collisions: 'KCJO' is also the Kansas City Jazz Orchestra; 'Miami' is also a Garifuna village near Tela, Honduras; 'Goombay' is also a historic Key West festival name (Fantasy Fest disambiguation). Lower-confidence facts from AI search summaries, not independently confirmed: bomba festival organizer (Afro Borinken Roots) and performers; Fiesta Maya organizer (Corn Maya Inc.). Rancho Bejucal guateque evidence dates from 2017; current status unknown. Museum of Miami artist-in-residence pages list program dates without years. Florida Memory, historymiamiarchives.org, Cultural Equity (Lomax) and the loc.gov search API blocked scripted access (403 or JS challenge); item-level loc.gov JSON worked. News items cited by headline only (from Google News RSS), with no direct article URL: Herald 2019 IFE-ILE, Herald 2023 Compas 25, WSVN Calle Ocho 48th, Sun Sentinel St. Catherine 49th, WLRN Miamibloco, Miami Times Overtown festival, Herald 2026 bomba gallery. URLs given are Google News searches.

[history] Miami 1896 incorporation vote: Wikipedia (Overtown) says 168 of 362 'colored'; other widely cited figures are 162 of 368 or 'about one-third'. Unresolved. Goombay founding year: 1976 (FIU News, Miami Herald) vs 1977 (WLRN, Coconut Grove Spotlight). Ervin Rouse death date: July 3, 1981 (NCpedia) vs July 8, 1981 (Wikipedia; UPI story dated July 8). Chubby Wise birthplace: St. Augustine (Wikipedia) vs Lake City (Florida Folk Heritage Award bio). Boca Raton Magazine calls Joni Mitchell '18 years old' in fall 1967; she was born in 1943 (23-24). 'If the Jasmine Don't Get You... the Bay Breeze Will' is a Vince Martin solo LP per Wikipedia (recorded Nashville 1969); Boca Mag calls it a Martin-Neil collaborative LP. Venue name varies: 'Gaslight South' (Luna Star bio), 'the Gaslight' (Boca Mag, New Times 2019), 'Gaslight Café' (New Times 2025; also the name of a NYC club). South Florida Folk Festival numbering inconsistent: 'inception in 1992' (club), '15th edition' Jan 2008 after 2-year gap (Sun-Sentinel), '20th anniversary' in 2014 (Acoustic Music Scene). Everglades Bluegrass numbering inconsistent: '30th' around 2008 (SFBA history) vs '49th' in Dec 2026 (SFBA site); first convention dated 1977 prep / 1978 flyer. South Florida Fair's 2026 contest page still says 'during the 2024 South Florida Fair' (template text); contest start year inferred. WLRN (2025) says Bahamian laborers settled in the Grove in the 'early 19th century'; FIU and Bucuvalas say late 1800s — WLRN likely wrong. Domains: miamibrowardcarnival.com hijacked by casino spam; compasfestival.com and scottishfestival.com parked; browardfolkclub.org does not resolve; dancefl.us and contradancinghollywood.com do not resolve. AI search summaries contained errors: called the 1935 Lomax/Hurston trip WPA (it was Library of Congress); listed Celia Cruz and Myrlande Constant as NEA Heritage Fellows (not on NEA FL list); named Indio Naborí and Celina González as Miami exile repentistas (both remained in Cuba). Unverified (single AI-summary source): Seminole Tribal Fair first year (1971?), Scottish highland games founding (1983), Miami Broward Carnival founding (1984) and attendance (50-75k). NEA state attribution reflects residence at award time (e.g., Hidalgo in Ocoee, Toth/Tsimouris in Tarpon Springs) — not metro. Research constraints: Wikipedia API and curl were rate-limited (used web_fetch instead); tunearch.org and some LOC/Miccosukee pages returned 403; Brave/Bing scraping blocked after a few queries.
